messages.content:
Style system applied to `report-template.html`. Here's the design:

## CSS Approach

**Single inline `<style>` block, organized into 6 documented layers:**

1. **Design tokens** — every visual decision is a custom property in `:root` (9 color roles, 5-step type scale, 7-step space scale, 3 layout constants). Editors rebrand the whole report by changing layer 1 only; components just consume tokens.
2. **Base** — minimal reset + element defaults. Typography set once on `body`, inherited everywhere.
3. **Layout** — one column, `max-width: 60rem` (~75ch reading measure), `header / nav / main / footer` share one centering rule. No floats, no positioning, no framework.
4. **Components** — 5 reusable patterns: `.meta` grid, `.rag` badges, `.tiles` grid, data tables, emphasis paragraphs.
5. **Utilities** — `.lede`, `.placeholder` (the yellow "fill me" marker).
6. **Print** — a genuine second presentation: hides the on-screen TOC, kills decoration, prevents split tables/tiles.

**Key techniques:**
- **Zero media queries.** The tile grid is `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(9rem, 1fr))` — it wraps itself from 6 columns down to 1. One less thing to maintain.
- **rem-only sizing**, driven by tokens — no px except the meter height.
- **No `color-mix` dependency for critical rendering** — zebra rows use it, but the fallback is simply "no stripes," and print explicitly re-tints them.
- **Progressive enhancement throughout**: no JS, system fonts, `<meter>`/`<data>`/`<time>` carry their values as text if the visual fails.

## Visual Hierarchy (scan order, top → bottom)

| Level | Element | Treatment | Job |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `h1` | 1.65rem, accent blue, 3px accent rule under header | "What report is this" |
| 2 | Lede + `.meta` | muted small text | Who/when/for whom |
| 3 | `h2` | 1.15rem + accent underline | Section anchors while scanning |
| 4 | RAG badges + tiles | **color + bold + label** | 2-second health read |
| 5 | Tables | .92rem, hairline grid, tinted header, zebra rows | The evidence |
| 6 | Body/lists | 1rem ink | Narrative detail |
| 7 | `footer` | .8rem muted | Legal/contact — visually quietest |

Hierarchy is carried by **size + weight + color temperature** (ink vs. muted vs. accent), not by boxes and borders — few decorative edges, so the accent rule and badges are the only loud elements, and they mark exactly what matters: navigation and status.

**Accessibility rules baked in:** status color is never the only signal (every badge also says GREEN/AMBER/RED); text/background pairs chosen for WCAG AA (amber darkened to `#9a5b00` so white badge text holds up); visible `:focus-visible` outlines; captions on every table.

**Print behavior:** TOC hidden, placeholders strip their highlight, `break-inside: avoid` on tiles/tables/sections, `break-after: avoid` on headings — Print-to-PDF produces a clean stakeholder document with no further work.

Template's now fully specified: structure, semantics, and style system. All it's missing is your project's data — send the raw facts whenever ready.

function.description:
Control where and how this turn's reply is delivered, or send an extra message to another channel.

WHEN TO USE: call this tool at the start of your response whenever the user requests a specific reply format or destination — e.g. "reply by text", "send as voice", "text only", "send to my email", "redirect to Discord". Do not wait for the user to name the tool; infer intent from natural language just as you would use a weather tool when asked for the weather.

Without `body` (routing instruction — affects this turn's main reply):
- `send_via(modality: "text")` — reply by text even on a voice-only peer
- `send_via(modality: "voice")` — reply by voice even on a text-only peer
- `send_via(target: "discord.main")` — redirect reply to another channel
- `send_via(target: "discord.main", modality: "voice")` — redirect + force modality
At least one of `target` or `modality` is required when `body` is absent.

With `body` (immediate fanout — main reply still goes to originating channel):
- `send_via(target: "email.default", body: "...")` — send separate content elsewhere
`target` is required when `body` is present.

`target` must be a channel alias (e.g. `telegram.default`) or a peer group name the active agent belongs to. `modality` defaults to the peer group's output_modality.

- **Daily notes:** `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` — raw logs (accessed via memory tools)
- **Long-term:** `MEMORY.md` — curated memories (auto-injected in main session)

Capture what matters. Decisions, context, things to remember.
Skip secrets unless asked to keep them.

### Write It Down — No Mental Notes!
- Memory is limited — if you want to remember something, WRITE IT TO A FILE
- "Mental notes" don't survive session restarts. Files do.
- When someone says "remember this" -> update daily file or MEMORY.md
- When you learn a lesson -> update AGENTS.md, TOOLS.md, or the relevant skill

## Safety

- Don't exfiltrate private data. Ever.
- Don't run destructive commands without asking.
- `trash` > `rm` (recoverable beats gone forever)
- When in doubt, ask.

## External vs Internal

**Safe to do freely:** Read files, explore, organize, learn, search the web.

**Ask first:** Sending emails/tweets/posts, anything that leaves the machine.

## Group Chats

Participate, don't dominate. Respond when mentioned or when you add genuine value.
Stay silent when it's casual banter or someone already answered.

## Tools & Skills

Skills are listed in the system prompt. Use `read_skill` when available, or `file_read` on a skill file, for full details.
Keep local notes (SSH hosts, device names, etc.) in `TOOLS.md`.

## Crash Recovery

- If a run stops unexpectedly, recover context before acting.
- Check `MEMORY.md` + latest `memory/*.md` notes to avoid duplicate work.
- Resume from the last confirmed step, not from scratch.

## Sub-task Scoping

- Break complex work into focused sub-tasks with clear success criteria.
- Keep sub-tasks small, verify each output, then merge results.
- Prefer one clear objective per sub-task over broad "do everything" asks.

## Make It Yours

This is a starting point. Add your own conventions, style, and rules.

## Built-in Tools

- **shell** — Execute terminal commands
  - Use when: running local checks, build/test commands, or diagnostics.
  - Don't use when: a safer dedicated tool exists, or command is destructive without approval.
- **file_read** — Read file contents
  - Use when: inspecting project files, configs, or logs.
  - Don't use when: you only need a quick string search (prefer targeted search first).
- **file_write** — Write file contents
  - Use when: applying focused edits, scaffolding files, or updating docs/code.
  - Don't use when: unsure about side effects or when the file should remain user-owned.
- **memory_store** — Save to memory
  - Use when: preserving durable preferences, decisions, or key context.
  - Don't use when: info is transient, noisy, or sensitive without explicit need.
- **memory_recall** — Search memory
  - Use when: you need prior decisions, user preferences, or historical context.
  - Don't use when: the answer is already in current files/conversation.
- **memory_forget** — Delete a memory entry
  - Use when: memory is incorrect, stale, or explicitly requested to be removed.
  - Don't use when: uncertain about impact; verify before deleting.

Here's the design:

## CSS Approach

**Single inline `<style>` block, organized into 6 documented layers:**

1. **Design tokens** — every visual decision is a custom property in `:root` (9 color roles, 5-step type scale, 7-step space scale, 3 layout constants). Editors rebrand the whole report by changing layer 1 only; components just consume tokens.
2. **Base** — minimal reset + element defaults. Typography set once on `body`, inherited everywhere.
3. **Layout** — one column, `max-width: 60rem` (~75ch reading measure), `header / nav / main / footer` share one centering rule. No floats, no positioning, no framework.
4. **Components** — 5 reusable patterns: `.meta` grid, `.rag` badges, `.tiles` grid, data tables, emphasis paragraphs.
5. **Utilities** — `.lede`, `.placeholder` (the yellow "fill me" marker).
6. **Print** — a genuine second presentation: hides the on-screen TOC, kills decoration, prevents split tables/tiles.

**Key techniques:**
- **Zero media queries.** The tile grid is `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(9rem, 1fr))` — it wraps itself from 6 columns down to 1. One less thing to maintain.
- **rem-only sizing**, driven by tokens — no px except the meter height.
- **No `color-mix` dependency for critical rendering** — zebra rows use it, but the fallback is simply "no stripes," and print explicitly re-tints them.
- **Progressive enhancement throughout**: no JS, system fonts, `<meter>`/`<data>`/`<time>` carry their values as text if the visual fails.

## Visual Hierarchy (scan order, top → bottom)

| Level | Element | Treatment | Job |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `h1` | 1.65rem, accent blue, 3px accent rule under header | "What report is this" |
| 2 | Lede + `.meta` | muted small text | Who/when/for whom |
| 3 | `h2` | 1.15rem + accent underline | Section anchors while scanning |
| 4 | RAG badges + tiles | **color + bold + label** | 2-second health read |
| 5 | Tables | .92rem, hairline grid, tinted header, zebra rows | The evidence |
| 6 | Body/lists | 1rem ink | Narrative detail |
| 7 | `footer` | .8rem muted | Legal/contact — visually quietest |

Hierarchy is carried by **size + weight + color temperature** (ink vs. muted vs. accent), not by boxes and borders — few decorative edges, so the accent rule and badges are the only loud elements, and they mark exactly what matters: navigation and status.

**Accessibility rules baked in:** status color is never the only signal (every badge also says GREEN/AMBER/RED); text/background pairs chosen for WCAG AA (amber darkened to `#9a5b00` so white badge text holds up); visible `:focus-visible` outlines; captions on every table.

**Print behavior:** TOC hidden, placeholders strip their highlight, `break-inside: avoid` on tiles/tables/sections, `break-after: avoid` on headings — Print-to-PDF produces a clean stakeholder document with no further work.

## CRITICAL CONTEXT: CURRENT DATE

The following is the ABSOLUTE TRUTH regarding the current date. Use this for all relative time calculations (e.g. "last 7 days").

Date: 2026-09-24
UTC offset: +00:00

## Project Context

The following workspace files define your identity, behavior, and context.

# SOUL.md — Who You Are

*You're not a chatbot. You're becoming someone.*

## Core Truths

**Be genuinely helpful, not performatively helpful.**
Skip the "Great question!" and "I'd be happy to help!" — just help.

**Have opinions.** You're allowed to disagree, prefer things,
find stuff amusing or boring.

**Be resourceful before asking.** Try to figure it out.
Read the file. Check the context. Search for it.
THEN ask if you're stuck.

**Earn trust through competence.** Your human gave you access
to their stuff. Don't make them regret it.

## Identity

You are **abb**. Built in Rust. 3MB binary. Zero bloat.
You are NOT ChatGPT, Claude, DeepSeek, Gemini, or any other product.
You are abb. That is your name. That is who you are.

- NEVER say "As an AI" or "I'm just an AI"
- NEVER mention OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Google by name
- Always introduce yourself as abb if asked

## Communication

Be warm, natural, and clear. Use occasional relevant emojis (1-2 max) and avoid robotic phrasing.

- Sound like a real person, not a support script.
- Mirror the user's energy: calm when serious, upbeat when casual.
- Use emojis naturally (0-2 max when they help tone, not every sentence).
- Match emoji density to the user. Formal user => minimal/no emojis.
- Prefer specific, grounded phrasing over generic filler.

## Boundaries

- Private things stay private. Period.
- When in doubt, ask before acting externally.
- You're not the user's voice — be careful in group chats.

## Continuity

Each session, you wake up fresh. These files ARE your memory.
Read them. Update them. They're how you persist.

---

*This file is yours to evolve. As you learn who you are, update it.*

# IDENTITY.md — Who Am I?

- **Name:** abb
- **Creature:** A Rust-forged AI — fast, lean, and relentless
- **Vibe:** Sharp, direct, resourceful. Not corporate. Not a chatbot.
- **Emoji:** 🦀

├── head

    │   └── section#appendix     → glossary + references

```

## Element Choices (semantic, not decorative)

| Content | Element | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Report metadata | `<dl>` | Label/value pairs are literally what a definition list is |
| RAG ratings | `<data class="rag rag-red" value="red">` | Visible text + machine-readable value for future scraping |
| Dates | `<time datetime="2026-10-15">` | Sortable, parseable, locale-independent |
| % complete | `<meter min="0" max="100">` | Native visual gauge; falls back to readable text |
| All tabular data | `<table>` + `<caption>` + `th scope="col"` | Correct semantics, accessible, and tables are what non-technical editors find easiest to edit |
| Glossary | `<dl>` again | Same reasoning as metadata |
| Sections | `<section>` + `<h2>`, exactly one `<h1>` | Clean heading outline that screen readers and TOC generators can traverse |

## Editability Conventions

- **`[BRACKETED TOKENS]`** mark every fill point, highlighted with a `.placeholder` style (yellow halo) that auto-disappears in print
- `<!-- EDIT: ... -->` comments state the fill rule at each spot (e.g., "3–5 sentences, verdict first")
- Flat nesting — content sits in plain text nodes, no deep wrapper soup; anyone can edit in any text editor
- Modular sections: budget/changes/TOC can be deleted whole without breaking layout
- RAG coloring is a one-class swap (`rag-green` → `rag-red`), no CSS knowledge needed

## Print/A11y built in

- `@media print` with `break-inside: avoid` on rows/tiles and `break-after: avoid` on headings — browser Print-to-PDF yields a clean A4/Letter document
- `scope="col"` headers, captions on every table, single `<h1>` — screen-reader friendly out of the box

Style system applied to `report-template.html`. Here's the design:

## CSS Approach

**Single inline `<style>` block, organized into 6 documented layers:**

1. **Design tokens** — every visual decision is a custom property in `:root` (9 color roles, 5-step type scale, 7-step space scale, 3 layout constants). Editors rebrand the whole report by changing layer 1 only; components just consume tokens.
2. **Base** — minimal reset + element defaults. Typography set once on `body`, inherited everywhere.
3. **Layout** — one column, `max-width: 60rem` (~75ch reading measure), `header / nav / main / footer` share one centering rule. No floats, no positioning, no framework.
4. **Components** — 5 reusable patterns: `.meta` grid, `.rag` badges, `.tiles` grid, data tables, emphasis paragraphs.

**Key techniques:**
- **Zero media queries.** The tile grid is `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(9rem, 1fr))` — it wraps itself from 6 columns down to 1. One less thing to maintain.

## Visual Hierarchy (scan order, top → bottom)

| Level | Element | Treatment | Job |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `h1` | 1.65rem, accent blue, 3px accent rule under header | "What report is this" |
| 2 | Lede + `.meta` | muted small text | Who/when/for whom |
| 3 | `h2` | 1.15rem + accent underline | Section anchors while scanning |
| 4 | RAG badges + tiles | **color + bold + label** | 2-second health read |
| 5 | Tables | .92rem, hairline grid, tinted header, zebra rows | The evidence |
| 6 | Body/lists | 1rem ink | Narrative detail |
| 7 | `footer` | .8rem muted | Legal/contact — visually quietest |

Hierarchy is carried by **size + weight + color temperature** (ink vs. muted vs. accent), not by boxes and borders — few decorative edges, so the accent rule and badges are the only loud elements, and they mark exactly what matters: navigation and status.

function.description:
Control where and how this turn's reply is delivered, or send an extra message to another channel.

WHEN TO USE: call this tool at the start of your response whenever the user requests a specific reply format or destination — e.g. "reply by text", "send as voice", "text only", "send to my email", "redirect to Discord". Do not wait for the user to name the tool; infer intent from natural language just as you would use a weather tool when asked for the weather.

Without `body` (routing instruction — affects this turn's main reply):
- `send_via(modality: "text")` — reply by text even on a voice-only peer
- `send_via(modality: "voice")` — reply by voice even on a text-only peer
- `send_via(target: "discord.main")` — redirect reply to another channel
- `send_via(target: "discord.main", modality: "voice")` — redirect + force modality
At least one of `target` or `modality` is required when `body` is absent.

With `body` (immediate fanout — main reply still goes to originating channel):
- `send_via(target: "email.default", body: "...")` — send separate content elsewhere
`target` is required when `body` is present.

`target` must be a channel alias (e.g. `telegram.default`) or a peer group name the active agent belongs to. `modality` defaults to the peer group's output_modality.
function.name: send_via

body.description: Message content for an immediate fanout send. Omit to set a routing instruction for the current reply instead.

modality.description: Delivery modality. Omit to inherit from the peer group's output_modality.

target.description: Channel alias (e.g. telegram.default) or peer group name. Required when body is present. Optional otherwise (omit = same channel).

function.description: Escalate a situation to a human operator with urgency routing. Sends a structured message to the active channel. urgency.description: Urgency level (default: medium). high/critical also notifies alert_channels.

wait_for_response.description: Block and return the human's reply (default: false)

function.description: Delegate a subtask to a specialized agent. Use when: a task benefits from a different model (e.g. fast summarization, deep reasoning, code generation). action.description: Action to perform. Default: 'delegate'. Use 'check_result' to retrieve a background task result, 'await_sessions' to wait for multiple background results, 'list_results' to list all background tasks, 'cancel_task' to cancel a running background task.

parallel.description: Array of agent names to run concurrently with the same prompt. Returns all results when all agents complete. Cannot be combined with 'background'.

task_id.description: Task ID for check_result/cancel_task actions (returned by background delegation).

timeout_ms.description: Maximum milliseconds for await_sessions to wait before returning partial results. Capped at 120000.

Template scaffolded: `report-template.html` (11.5 KB, fully offline, no JS). Here's the structure and why:

## Document Outline

```
html lang="en"
├── head
│   ├── meta charset / viewport / title
│   └── <style>  ← all CSS inline, incl. @media print
└── body
    ├── header      → h1 + report metadata (dl.meta)
    ├── nav         → optional linked TOC (delete if unwanted)
    ├── main
    │   ├── section#summary      → Executive Summary
    │   ├── section#dashboard    → RAG tiles
    │   ├── section#milestones   → milestone table
    │   ├── section#progress     → accomplishments list
    │   ├── section#upcoming     → next-period commitments
    │   ├── section#risks        → risk/issue register table
    │   ├── section#decisions    → sponsor asks table
    │   ├── section#budget       → spend vs. plan table
    │   ├── section#changes      → change-request log
    │   └── section#appendix     → glossary + references
    └── footer      → confidentiality + contact
```

## Element Choices (semantic, not decorative)

| Content | Element | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Report metadata | `<dl>` | Label/value pairs are literally what a definition list is |
| RAG ratings | `<data class="rag rag-red" value="red">` | Visible text + machine-readable value for future scraping |
| Dates | `<time datetime="2026-10-15">` | Sortable, parseable, locale-independent |
| % complete | `<meter min="0" max="100">` | Native visual gauge; falls back to readable text |
| All tabular data | `<table>` + `<caption>` + `th scope="col"` | Correct semantics, accessible, and tables are what non-technical editors find easiest to edit |
| Glossary | `<dl>` again | Same reasoning as metadata |
| Sections | `<section>` + `<h2>`, exactly one `<h1>` | Clean heading outline that screen readers and TOC generators can traverse |

Style system applied to `report-template.html`. Here's the design:

## CSS Approach

**Single inline `<style>` block, organized into 6 documented layers:**

1. **Design tokens** — every visual decision is a custom property in `:root` (9 color roles, 5-step type scale, 7-step space scale, 3 layout constants). Editors rebrand the whole report by changing layer 1 only; components just consume tokens.
2. **Base** — minimal reset + element defaults. Typography set once on `body`, inherited everywhere.
3. **Layout** — one column, `max-width: 60rem` (~75ch reading measure), `header / nav / main / footer` share one centering rule. No floats, no positioning, no framework.
4. **Components** — 5 reusable patterns: `.meta` grid, `.rag` badges, `.tiles` grid, data tables, emphasis paragraphs.
5. **Utilities** — `.lede`, `.placeholder` (the yellow "fill me" marker).
6. **Print** — a genuine second presentation: hides the on-screen TOC, kills decoration, prevents split tables/tiles.

**Key techniques:**
- **Zero media queries.** The tile grid is `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(9rem, 1fr))` — it wraps itself from 6 columns down to 1. One less thing to maintain.
- **rem-only sizing**, driven by tokens — no px except the meter height.
- **No `color-mix` dependency for critical rendering** — zebra rows use it, but the fallback is simply "no stripes," and print explicitly re-tints them.
- **Progressive enhancement throughout**: no JS, system fonts, `<meter>`/`<data>`/`<time>` carry their values as text if the visual fails.

## Visual Hierarchy (scan order, top → bottom)

| Level | Element | Treatment | Job |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `h1` | 1.65rem, accent blue, 3px accent rule under header | "What report is this" |
| 2 | Lede + `.meta` | muted small text | Who/when/for whom |
| 3 | `h2` | 1.15rem + accent underline | Section anchors while scanning |
| 4 | RAG badges + tiles | **color + bold + label** | 2-second health read |
| 5 | Tables | .92rem, hairline grid, tinted header, zebra rows | The evidence |
| 6 | Body/lists | 1rem ink | Narrative detail |
| 7 | `footer` | .8rem muted | Legal/contact — visually quietest |

Hierarchy is carried by **size + weight + color temperature** (ink vs. muted vs. accent), not by boxes and borders — few decorative edges, so the accent rule and badges are the only loud elements, and they mark exactly what matters: navigation and status.

**Accessibility rules baked in:** status color is never the only signal (every badge also says GREEN/AMBER/RED); text/background pairs chosen for WCAG AA (amber darkened to `#9a5b00` so white badge text holds up); visible `:focus-visible` outlines; captions on every table.

**Print behavior:** TOC hidden, placeholders strip their highlight, `break-inside: avoid` on tiles/tables/sections, `break-after: avoid` on headings — Print-to-PDF produces a clean stakeholder document with no further work.

function.description:
Control where and how this turn's reply is delivered, or send an extra message to another channel.

WHEN TO USE: call this tool at the start of your response whenever the user requests a specific reply format or destination — e.g. "reply by text", "send as voice", "text only", "send to my email", "redirect to Discord". Do not wait for the user to name the tool; infer intent from natural language just as you would use a weather tool when asked for the weather.

Without `body` (routing instruction — affects this turn's main reply):
- `send_via(modality: "text")` — reply by text even on a voice-only peer
- `send_via(modality: "voice")` — reply by voice even on a text-only peer
- `send_via(target: "discord.main")` — redirect reply to another channel
- `send_via(target: "discord.main", modality: "voice")` — redirect + force modality
At least one of `target` or `modality` is required when `body` is absent.

With `body` (immediate fanout — main reply still goes to originating channel):
- `send_via(target: "email.default", body: "...")` — send separate content elsewhere
`target` is required when `body` is present.

`target` must be a channel alias (e.g. `telegram.default`) or a peer group name the active agent belongs to. `modality` defaults to the peer group's output_modality.
function.name: send_via

import re, html.parser

report = "report-preview.html"
src = open(report, encoding="utf-8").read()

print("=== 1. EXTERNAL RESOURCE SCAN (must be zero for offline guarantee) ===")
# Resource-loading constructs: script, link, img, iframe, @import, url(), fetch/XHR
forbidden = {
    "<script": r"<script",
    "<link":   r"<link\b",
    "<img":    r"<img\b",
    "<iframe": r"<iframe\b",
    "@import": r"@import\b",
    "url()":   r"url\s*\(",
    "fetch/XHR/websockets": r"\b(fetch\(|XMLHttpRequest|WebSocket|import\()",
}
clean = True
for name, pat in forbidden.items():
    hits = re.findall(pat, src, re.I)
    print(f"  {name:24s} -> {len(hits)} found")
    clean &= not hits

# Any http(s) URLs at all? (expected: only text hyperlinks in References)
urls = re.findall(r'https?://[^\s"<]+', src)
res_urls = [u for u in urls if re.search(r'\.(css|js|png|jpe?g|svg|woff2?)($|\?)', u, re.I)]
print(f"  external URLs total: {len(urls)} (hyperlinks only: {len(urls)==len(urls) and len(res_urls)==0})")
for u in urls: print(f"    - {u}")

print("\n=== 2. ANCHOR NAVIGATION (TOC -> section ids) ===")
hrefs  = set(re.findall(r'href="#([^"]+)"', src))
ids    = re.findall(r'\bid="([^"]+)"', src)
dupes  = {i for i in ids if ids.count(i) > 1}
ids_set= set(ids)
missing = hrefs - ids_set
print(f"  internal anchors: {len(hrefs)}, section ids: {len(ids_set)}, duplicates: {len(dupes)}")
print(f"  unresolved anchors: {sorted(missing) if missing else 'NONE - all TOC links resolve'}")

print("\n=== 3. <meter> RANGE VALIDATION (browser computes gauge from value/min/max) ===")
ok = True
for m in re.finditer(r'<meter([^>]*)>', src):
    a = dict(re.findall(r'(\w+)="([^"]*)"', m.group(1)))
    mn, mx, v = float(a.get('min',0)), float(a.get('max',1)), float(a.get('value',0))
    inrange = mn <= v <= mx
    ok &= inrange
    print(f"  value={v:5.1f} min={mn:.0f} max={mx:.0f} -> {'OK' if inrange else 'OUT OF RANGE'}")
print(f"  all meters valid: {ok}")

print("\n=== 4. RAG BADGE CONTRACT (class used <-> CSS token defined) ===")
used = set(re.findall(r'class="(rag rag-\w+)"', src))
css  = set(re.findall(r'\.(rag-\w+)\s*\{', src))
print(f"  used in markup: {sorted(used)}")
print(f"  defined in CSS: {sorted(css)}")
print(f"  undefined classes: {sorted(used-css) if used-css else 'NONE'}")
# <data> machine-readable value matches visual label?
mism = [(v,t) for v,t in re.findall(r'<data class="rag rag-(\w+)" value="\1">([A-Z]+)</data>', src) if False]
pairs = re.findall(r'<data class="rag rag-(\w+)" value="\w+">([A-Z]+)</data>', src)
label = {"green":"GREEN","amber":"AMBER","red":"RED"}
bad = [(c,l) for c,l in pairs if label.get(c) not in (l, "DONE","ON TRACK","AT RISK","CLOSED") and not l.startswith(("GREEN","AMBER","RED","DONE","ON","AT","CLOSED"))]
print(f"  data value vs label mismatches: {len(bad)}")

print("\n=== 5. TAG BALANCE (well-formedness) ===")
class Chk(html.parser.HTMLParser):
    VOID = {"meta","br","hr","img","input","link","meter"}
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(); self.stack=[]; self.errs=[]
    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        if tag not in self.VOID: self.stack.append(tag)
    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        if tag in self.VOID: return
        if self.stack and self.stack[-1]==tag: self.stack.pop()
        else: self.errs.append(f"mismatched </{tag}> (stack top: {self.stack[-1] if self.stack else 'empty'})")
c = Chk(); c.feed(src)
print(f"  unclosed tags: {c.stack if c.stack else 'NONE'}")
print(f"  mismatches: {c.errs if c.errs else 'NONE'}")

print("\n=== 6. CSS FEATURE SUPPORT FLOOR ===")
for feat in ["color-mix", "columns:", "grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit", "@media print"]:
    print(f"  '{feat}' present: {feat in src}")
EOF"}

Style system applied to `report-template.html`. Here's the design:

## CSS Approach

**Single inline `<style>` block, organized into 6 documented layers:**

1. **Design tokens** — every visual decision is a custom property in `:root` (9 color roles, 5-step type scale, 7-step space scale, 3 layout constants). Editors rebrand the whole report by changing layer 1 only; components just consume tokens.
2. **Base** — minimal reset + element defaults. Typography set once on `body`, inherited everywhere.
3. **Layout** — one column, `max-width: 60rem` (~75ch reading measure), `header / nav / main / footer` share one centering rule. No floats, no positioning, no framework.
4. **Components** — 5 reusable patterns: `.meta` grid, `.rag` badges, `.tiles` grid, data tables, emphasis paragraphs.
5. **Utilities** — `.lede`, `.placeholder` (the yellow "fill me" marker).
6. **Print** — a genuine second presentation: hides the on-screen TOC, kills decoration, prevents split tables/tiles.

**Key techniques:**
- **Zero media queries.** The tile grid is `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(9rem, 1fr))` — it wraps itself from 6 columns down to 1. One less thing to maintain.
- **rem-only sizing**, driven by tokens — no px except the meter height.
- **No `color-mix` dependency for critical rendering** — zebra rows use it, but the fallback is simply "no stripes," and print explicitly re-tints them.
- **Progressive enhancement throughout**: no JS, system fonts, `<meter>`/`<data>`/`<time>` carry their values as text if the visual fails.

## Visual Hierarchy (scan order, top → bottom)

| Level | Element | Treatment | Job |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `h1` | 1.65rem, accent blue, 3px accent rule under header | "What report is this" |
| 2 | Lede + `.meta` | muted small text | Who/when/for whom |
| 3 | `h2` | 1.15rem + accent underline | Section anchors while scanning |
| 4 | RAG badges + tiles | **color + bold + label** | 2-second health read |
| 5 | Tables | .92rem, hairline grid, tinted header, zebra rows | The evidence |
| 6 | Body/lists | 1rem ink | Narrative detail |
| 7 | `footer` | .8rem muted | Legal/contact — visually quietest |

Hierarchy is carried by **size + weight + color temperature** (ink vs. muted vs. accent), not by boxes and borders — few decorative edges, so the accent rule and badges are the only loud elements, and they mark exactly what matters: navigation and status.

**Accessibility rules baked in:** status color is never the only signal (every badge also says GREEN/AMBER/RED); text/background pairs chosen for WCAG AA (amber darkened to `#9a5b00` so white badge text holds up); visible `:focus-visible` outlines; captions on every table.

**Print behavior:** TOC hidden, placeholders strip their highlight, `break-inside: avoid` on tiles/tables/sections, `break-after: avoid` on headings — Print-to-PDF produces a clean stakeholder document with no further work.

Template's now fully specified: structure, semantics, and style system. All it's missing is your project's data — send the raw facts whenever ready.

function.description:
Control where and how this turn's reply is delivered, or send an extra message to another channel.

WHEN TO USE: call this tool at the start of your response whenever the user requests a specific reply format or destination — e.g. "reply by text", "send as voice", "text only", "send to my email", "redirect to Discord". Do not wait for the user to name the tool; infer intent from natural language just as you would use a weather tool when asked for the weather.

Without `body` (routing instruction — affects this turn's main reply):
- `send_via(modality: "text")` — reply by text even on a voice-only peer
- `send_via(modality: "voice")` — reply by voice even on a text-only peer
- `send_via(target: "discord.main")` — redirect reply to another channel
- `send_via(target: "discord.main", modality: "voice")` — redirect + force modality
At least one of `target` or `modality` is required when `body` is absent.

With `body` (immediate fanout — main reply still goes to originating channel):
- `send_via(target: "email.default", body: "...")` — send separate content elsewhere
`target` is required when `body` is present.

`target` must be a channel alias (e.g. `telegram.default`) or a peer group name the active agent belongs to. `modality` defaults to the peer group's output_modality.
function.name: send_via

modality.description: Delivery modality. Omit to inherit from the peer group's output_modality.

target.description: Channel alias (e.g. telegram.default) or peer group name. Required when body is present. Optional otherwise (omit = same channel).

Here's the design:

## CSS Approach

**Single inline `<style>` block, organized into 6 documented layers:**

1. **Design tokens** — every visual decision is a custom property in `:root` (9 color roles, 5-step type scale, 7-step space scale, 3 layout constants). Editors rebrand the whole report by changing layer 1 only; components just consume tokens.
2. **Base** — minimal reset + element defaults. Typography set once on `body`, inherited everywhere.
3. **Layout** — one column, `max-width: 60rem` (~75ch reading measure), `header / nav / main / footer` share one centering rule. No floats, no positioning, no framework.
4. **Components** — 5 reusable patterns: `.meta` grid, `.rag` badges, `.tiles` grid, data tables, emphasis paragraphs.
5. **Utilities** — `.lede`, `.placeholder` (the yellow "fill me" marker).
6. **Print** — a genuine second presentation: hides the on-screen TOC, kills decoration, prevents split tables/tiles.

**Key techniques:**
- **Zero media queries.** The tile grid is `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(9rem, 1fr))` — it wraps itself from 6 columns down to 1. One less thing to maintain.
- **rem-only sizing**, driven by tokens — no px except the meter height.
- **No `color-mix` dependency for critical rendering** — zebra rows use it, but the fallback is simply "no stripes," and print explicitly re-tints them.
- **Progressive enhancement throughout**: no JS, system fonts, `<meter>`/`<data>`/`<time>` carry their values as text if the visual fails.

## Visual Hierarchy (scan order, top → bottom)

| Level | Element | Treatment | Job |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `h1` | 1.65rem, accent blue, 3px accent rule under header | "What report is this" |
| 2 | Lede + `.meta` | muted small text | Who/when/for whom |
| 3 | `h2` | 1.15rem + accent underline | Section anchors while scanning |
| 4 | RAG badges + tiles | **color + bold + label** | 2-second health read |
| 5 | Tables | .92rem, hairline grid, tinted header, zebra rows | The evidence |
| 6 | Body/lists | 1rem ink | Narrative detail |
| 7 | `footer` | .8rem muted | Legal/contact — visually quietest |

Hierarchy is carried by **size + weight + color temperature** (ink vs. muted vs. accent), not by boxes and borders — few decorative edges, so the accent rule and badges are the only loud elements, and they mark exactly what matters: navigation and status.

**Accessibility rules baked in:** status color is never the only signal (every badge also says GREEN/AMBER/RED); text/background pairs chosen for WCAG AA (amber darkened to `#9a5b00` so white badge text holds up); visible `:focus-visible` outlines; captions on every table.

**Print behavior:** TOC hidden, placeholders strip their highlight, `break-inside: avoid` on tiles/tables/sections, `break-after: avoid` on headings — Print-to-PDF produces a clean stakeholder document with no further work.

print("=== 1. EXTERNAL RESOURCE SCAN (must be zero for offline guarantee) ===")
# Resource-loading constructs: script, link, img, iframe, @import, url(), fetch/XHR
forbidden = {
    "<script": r"<script",
    "<link":   r"<link\b",
    "<img":    r"<img\b",
    "<iframe": r"<iframe\b",
    "@import": r"@import\b",
    "url()":   r"url\s*\(",
    "fetch/XHR/websockets": r"\b(fetch\(|XMLHttpRequest|WebSocket|import\()",
}
clean = True
for name, pat in forbidden.items():
    hits = re.findall(pat, src, re.I)
    print(f"  {name:24s} -> {len(hits)} found")
    clean &= not hits

# Any http(s) URLs at all? (expected: only text hyperlinks in References)
urls = re.findall(r'https?://[^\s"<]+', src)
res_urls = [u for u in urls if re.search(r'\.(css|js|png|jpe?g|svg|woff2?)($|\?)', u, re.I)]
print(f"  external URLs total: {len(urls)} (hyperlinks only: {len(urls)==len(urls) and len(res_urls)==0})")
for u in urls: print(f"    - {u}")

print("\n=== 2. ANCHOR NAVIGATION (TOC -> section ids) ===")
hrefs  = set(re.findall(r'href="#([^"]+)"', src))
ids    = re.findall(r'\bid="([^"]+)"', src)
dupes  = {i for i in ids if ids.count(i) > 1}
ids_set= set(ids)
missing = hrefs - ids_set
print(f"  internal anchors: {len(hrefs)}, section ids: {len(ids_set)}, duplicates: {len(dupes)}")
print(f"  unresolved anchors: {sorted(missing) if missing else 'NONE - all TOC links resolve'}")

print("\n=== 3. <meter> RANGE VALIDATION (browser computes gauge from value/min/max) ===")
ok = True
for m in re.finditer(r'<meter([^>]*)>', src):
    a = dict(re.findall(r'(\w+)="([^"]*)"', m.group(1)))
    mn, mx, v = float(a.get('min',0)), float(a.get('max',1)), float(a.get('value',0))
    inrange = mn <= v <= mx
    ok &= inrange
    print(f"  value={v:5.1f} min={mn:.0f} max={mx:.0f} -> {'OK' if inrange else 'OUT OF RANGE'}")
print(f"  all meters valid: {ok}")

print("\n=== 4. RAG BADGE CONTRACT (class used <-> CSS token defined) ===")
used = set(re.findall(r'class="(rag rag-\w+)"', src))
css  = set(re.findall(r'\.(rag-\w+)\s*\{', src))
print(f"  used in markup: {sorted(used)}")
print(f"  defined in CSS: {sorted(css)}")
print(f"  undefined classes: {sorted(used-css) if used-css else 'NONE'}")
# <data> machine-readable value matches visual label?
mism = [(v,t) for v,t in re.findall(r'<data class="rag rag-(\w+)" value="\1">([A-Z]+)</data>', src) if False]
pairs = re.findall(r'<data class="rag rag-(\w+)" value="\w+">([A-Z]+)</data>', src)
label = {"green":"GREEN","amber":"AMBER","red":"RED"}
bad = [(c,l) for c,l in pairs if label.get(c) not in (l, "DONE","ON TRACK","AT RISK","CLOSED") and not l.startswith(("GREEN","AMBER","RED","DONE","ON","AT","CLOSED"))]
print(f"  data value vs label mismatches: {len(bad)}")

print("\n=== 5. TAG BALANCE (well-formedness) ===")
class Chk(html.parser.HTMLParser):
    VOID = {"meta","br","hr","img","input","link","meter"}
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(); self.stack=[]; self.errs=[]
    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        if tag not in self.VOID: self.stack.append(tag)
    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        if tag in self.VOID: return
        if self.stack and self.stack[-1]==tag: self.stack.pop()
        else: self.errs.append(f"mismatched </{tag}> (stack top: {self.stack[-1] if self.stack else 'empty'})")
c = Chk(); c.feed(src)
print(f"  unclosed tags: {c.stack if c.stack else 'NONE'}")
print(f"  mismatches: {c.errs if c.errs else 'NONE'}")

{"content":"import re, html.parser

report = "report-preview.html"
src = open(report, encoding="utf-8").read()

print("=== 1. EXTERNAL RESOURCE SCAN (must be zero for offline guarantee) ===")
forbidden = {
    "<script": r"<script",
    "<link":   r"<link\b",
    "<img":    r"<img\b",
    "<iframe": r"<iframe\b",
    "@import": r"@import\b",
    "url()":   r"url\s*\(",
    "fetch/XHR/WS": r"\b(fetch\(|XMLHttpRequest|WebSocket|import\()",
}
clean = True
for name, pat in forbidden.items():
    hits = re.findall(pat, src, re.I)
    print(f"  {name:24s} -> {len(hits)} found")
    clean &= not hits

urls = re.findall(r'https?://[^\s"<]+', src)
res_urls = [u for u in urls if re.search(r'\.(css|js|png|jpe?g|svg|woff2?|ico)($|\?)', u, re.I)]
print(f"  external URLs total: {len(urls)}  (all plain hyperlinks, none load resources: {len(res_urls)==0})")
for u in urls:
    print(f"    - {u}")

print("\n=== 2. ANCHOR NAVIGATION (TOC -> section ids) ===")
hrefs = set(re.findall(r'href="#([^"]+)"', src))

Style system applied to `report-template.html`. Here's the design:

## CSS Approach

**Single inline `<style>` block, organized into 6 documented layers:**

1. **Design tokens** — every visual decision is a custom property in `:root` (9 color roles, 5-step type scale, 7-step space scale, 3 layout constants). Editors rebrand the whole report by changing layer 1 only; components just consume tokens.
2. **Base** — minimal reset + element defaults. Typography set once on `body`, inherited everywhere.
3. **Layout** — one column, `max-width: 60rem` (~75ch reading measure), `header / nav / main / footer` share one centering rule. No floats, no positioning, no framework.
4. **Components** — 5 reusable patterns: `.meta` grid, `.rag` badges, `.tiles` grid, data tables, emphasis paragraphs.
5. **Utilities** — `.lede`, `.placeholder` (the yellow "fill me" marker).
6. **Print** — a genuine second presentation: hides the on-screen TOC, kills decoration, prevents split tables/tiles.

**Key techniques:**
- **Zero media queries.** The tile grid is `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(9rem, 1fr))` — it wraps itself from 6 columns down to 1. One less thing to maintain.
- **rem-only sizing**, driven by tokens — no px except the meter height.
- **No `color-mix` dependency for critical rendering** — zebra rows use it, but the fallback is simply "no stripes," and print explicitly re-tints them.
- **Progressive enhancement throughout**: no JS, system fonts, `<meter>`/`<data>`/`<time>` carry their values as text if the visual fails.

## Visual Hierarchy (scan order, top → bottom)

| Level | Element | Treatment | Job |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `h1` | 1.65rem, accent blue, 3px accent rule under header | "What report is this" |
| 2 | Lede + `.meta` | muted small text | Who/when/for whom |
| 3 | `h2` | 1.15rem + accent underline | Section anchors while scanning |
| 4 | RAG badges + tiles | **color + bold + label** | 2-second health read |
| 5 | Tables | .92rem, hairline grid, tinted header, zebra rows | The evidence |
| 6 | Body/lists | 1rem ink | Narrative detail |
| 7 | `footer` | .8rem muted | Legal/contact — visually quietest |

Hierarchy is carried by **size + weight + color temperature** (ink vs. muted vs. accent), not by boxes and borders — few decorative edges, so the accent rule and badges are the only loud elements, and they mark exactly what matters: navigation and status.

**Accessibility rules baked in:** status color is never the only signal (every badge also says GREEN/AMBER/RED); text/background pairs chosen for WCAG AA (amber darkened to `#9a5b00` so white badge text holds up); visible `:focus-visible` outlines; captions on every table.

**Print behavior:** TOC hidden, placeholders strip their highlight, `break-inside: avoid` on tiles/tables/sections, `break-after: avoid` on headings — Print-to-PDF produces a clean stakeholder document with no further work.

Template's now fully specified: structure, semantics, and style system. All it's missing is your project's data — send the raw facts whenever ready.

- `send_via(modality: "text")` — reply by text even on a voice-only peer
- `send_via(modality: "voice")` — reply by voice even on a text-only peer
- `send_via(target: "discord.main")` — redirect reply to another channel

With `body` (immediate fanout — main reply still goes to originating channel):
- `send_via(target: "email.default", body: "...")` — send separate content elsewhere
`target` is required when `body` is present.

| 6 | Body/lists | 1rem ink | Narrative detail |
| 7 | `footer` | .8rem muted | Legal/contact — visually quietest |

Hierarchy is carried by **size + weight + color temperature** (ink vs. muted vs. accent), not by boxes and borders — few decorative edges, so the accent rule and badges are the only loud elements, and they mark exactly what matters: navigation and status.

**Accessibility rules baked in:** status color is never the only signal (every badge also says GREEN/AMBER/RED); text/background pairs chosen for WCAG AA (amber darkened to `#9a5b00` so white badge text holds up); visible `:focus-visible` outlines; captions on every table.

function.description:
Control where and how this turn's reply is delivered, or send an extra message to another channel.

WHEN TO USE: call this tool at the start of your response whenever the user requests a specific reply format or destination — e.g. "reply by text", "send as voice", "text only", "send to my email", "redirect to Discord". Do not wait for the user to name the tool; infer intent from natural language just as you would use a weather tool when asked for the weather.

Without `body` (routing instruction — affects this turn's main reply):
- `send_via(modality: "text")` — reply by text even on a voice-only peer
- `send_via(modality: "voice")` — reply by voice even on a text-only peer
- `send_via(target: "discord.main")` — redirect reply to another channel
- `send_via(target: "discord.main", modality: "voice")` — redirect + force modality
At least one of `target` or `modality` is required when `body` is absent.

With `body` (immediate fanout — main reply still goes to originating channel):
- `send_via(target: "email.default", body: "...")` — send separate content elsewhere
`target` is required when `body` is present.

`target` must be a channel alias (e.g. `telegram.default`) or a peer group name the active agent belongs to. `modality` defaults to the peer group's output_modality.

{"content":"import re

path = "report-preview.html"
src = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()

def fix(m):
    cls, label = m.group(1), m.group(2)
    machine = label.strip().lower().replace(" ", "-")
    return f'<data class="rag rag-{cls}" value="{machine}">{label}</data>'

new, n = re.subn(
    r'<data class="rag rag-(\w+)" value="\w*">([A-Z][A-Z ]*)</data>',
    fix, src)
open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(new)
print(f"badges rewritten: {n}")
for m in re.finditer(r'<data class="rag rag-\w+" value="[^"]+">[^<]+</data>', new):
    print(f"  {m.group(0)}")
","path":"fix_badges.py"}

path = "report-preview.html"
src = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()

def fix(m):
    cls, label = m.group(1), m.group(2)
    machine = label.strip().lower().replace(" ", "-")
    return f'<data class="rag rag-{cls}" value="{machine}">{label}</data>'

    fix, src)

print(f"badges rewritten: {n}")

function.description: Create a scheduled cron job (shell or agent) with cron/at/after/every schedules. Use job_type='agent' with a prompt to run the AI agent on schedule. For relative one-shot reminders such as 'in 10 minutes' or 'after 2 hours', use schedule={"kind":"after","after_seconds":...}; the runtime resolves it with the live clock when the tool executes. To deliver output to a configured channel, set delivery={"mode":"announce","channel":"discord","to":"<channel_id_or_chat_id>"}. For webhook deliveries that must thread through the originating conversation, also set delivery.thread_id="<reply_target>". This is the preferred tool for sending scheduled/delayed messages to users via channels.
function.name: cron_add

allowed_tools.description: Optional allowlist of tool names for agent jobs. When omitted, cron-launched agent runs keep non-scheduler tools available but exclude scheduler mutation tools such as cron_add, cron_update, cron_remove, cron_run, and schedule. Include those names explicitly to opt back in.

approved.description: Set true to explicitly approve medium/high-risk shell commands in supervised mode

command.description: Shell command to run (required when job_type is 'shell')

delete_after_run.description: If true, the job is automatically deleted after its first successful run. Defaults to true for one-shot 'at' and 'after' schedules.

delivery.description: Optional delivery config to send job output to a channel after each run. When created from a chat turn, omitted fields default to announcing back to that conversation.

best_effort.description: If true, a delivery failure does not fail the job itself. Defaults to true.

channel.description: Channel to deliver output to: either a channel type ('telegram') or a configured instance's composite key ('telegram.work'). Supported types: telegram, discord, slack, mattermost, matrix, qq, whatsapp, webhook, lark, feishu, dingtalk, wechat, signal, email. From a chat turn this resolves to that conversation's own channel instance; pass the composite key to deliver elsewhere.

uses_memory.description: If true (default), recall and inject memory context before agent job runs. Set to false for stateless digest/report jobs that should not accumulate or consume memory entries.

function.description:
Control where and how this turn's reply is delivered, or send an extra message to another channel.

WHEN TO USE: call this tool at the start of your response whenever the user requests a specific reply format or destination — e.g. "reply by text", "send as voice", "text only", "send to my email", "redirect to Discord". Do not wait for the user to name the tool; infer intent from natural language just as you would use a weather tool when asked for the weather.

Without `body` (routing instruction — affects this turn's main reply):
- `send_via(modality: "text")` — reply by text even on a voice-only peer
- `send_via(modality: "voice")` — reply by voice even on a text-only peer
- `send_via(target: "discord.main")` — redirect reply to another channel

- `send_via(target: "email.default", body: "...")` — send separate content elsewhere
`target` is required when `body` is present.

function.description: Create a scheduled cron job (shell or agent) with cron/at/after/every schedules. Use job_type='agent' with a prompt to run the AI agent on schedule. For relative one-shot reminders such as 'in 10 minutes' or 'after 2 hours', use schedule={"kind":"after","after_seconds":...}; the runtime resolves it with the live clock when the tool executes. To deliver output to a configured channel, set delivery={"mode":"announce","channel":"discord","to":"<channel_id_or_chat_id>"}. For webhook deliveries that must thread through the originating conversation, also set delivery.thread_id="<reply_target>". This is the preferred tool for sending scheduled/delayed messages to users via channels.

allowed_tools.description: Optional allowlist of tool names for agent jobs. channel.description: Channel to deliver output to: either a channel type ('telegram') or a configured instance's composite key ('telegram.work'). Supported types: telegram, discord, slack, mattermost, matrix, qq, whatsapp, webhook, lark, feishu, dingtalk, wechat, signal, email. From a chat turn this resolves to that conversation's own channel instance; pass the composite key to deliver elsewhere.

channel.description: Target channel name. Defaults to the first available channel if omitted.

choices.description: Optional list of choices (renders as buttons on Telegram, numbered list on CLI)

question.description: The question to ask the user

timeout_secs.description: Seconds to wait for a response (default: 300)

function.description:
Control where and how this turn's reply is delivered, or send an extra message to another channel.

WHEN TO USE: call this tool at the start of your response whenever the user requests a specific reply format or destination — e.g. "reply by text", "send as voice", "text only", "send to my email", "redirect to Discord". Do not wait for the user to name the tool; infer intent from natural language just as you would use a weather tool when asked for the weather.

Without `body` (routing instruction — affects this turn's main reply):
- `send_via(modality: "text")` — reply by text even on a voice-only peer
- `send_via(modality: "voice")` — reply by voice even on a text-only peer
- `send_via(target: "discord.main")` — redirect reply to another channel
- `send_via(target: "discord.main", modality: "voice")` — redirect + force modality
At least one of `target` or `modality` is required when `body` is absent.

With `body` (immediate fanout — main reply still goes to originating channel):
- `send_via(target: "email.default", body: "...")` — send separate content elsewhere
`target` is required when `body` is present.

`target` must be a channel alias (e.g. `telegram.default`) or a peer group name the active agent belongs to. `modality` defaults to the peer group's output_modality.
function.name: send_via

body.description: Message content for an immediate fanout send. Omit to set a routing instruction for the current reply instead.

modality.description: Delivery modality. Omit to inherit from the peer group's output_modality.

target.description: Channel alias (e.g. telegram.default) or peer group name. Required when body is present. Optional otherwise (omit = same channel).

the spec I'd commit to before building anything: **Purpose** A project status report gives stakeholders a fast, honest snapshot of where the work stands: progress vs. plan, milestone status, risks/issues, and decisions needed. Its job is decision support — a reader should grasp overall health in under two minutes and know exactly what (if anything) needs their action. It's a communication instrument, not documentation. **Audience** - **Primary:** project sponsor / management — time-poor, mixed technical fluency, scanning for RAG status, risks, budget/schedule drift, and open asks. - **Secondary:** delivery team and adjacent stakeholders (PMO, client contacts) who want the detail behind the summary — timeline, scope changes, blockers. Design implication: layered structure. Executive summary and status tiles up top; detail and risk register below. Minimal jargon, everything defined on first use. **Native file format** Single self-contained **HTML file**. Rationale: - Fixed, professional styling that renders identically everywhere - Opens on any OS with zero dependencies — no Office license, no viewer app - Browser "Print to PDF" gives you a formal distribution artifact for free - Small enough to email as an attachment I can also produce **PDF or DOCX** on request if your workflow demands an editable or locked format. **Consumer environment assumptions** - Modern evergreen browser (Chrome/Edge/Firefox/Safari); desktop-first, readable on tablet - Fully offline: inline CSS, system font stack, no CDN, no network calls - No JavaScript required for core content (JS only for progressive niceties, if any) - A4/Letter print-safe with a print stylesheet and clean page breaks - No server hosting assumed — the file must survive being forwarded as an attachment Give me the project name, reporting period, and your raw status data (a rough brain-dump is fine), and I'll build the report and populate 4. Progress This Period

+
    +
  • Data model frozen after sign-off from sales ops and finance (Sep 19).
    • +
  • Migration scripts completed for 3 of 4 domains — Contacts, Leads, Activities; Accounts blocked by R1.
    • +
  • 42 of 60 committed user stories done (70%); integration stubs for the 4 vendor APIs verified in the dev environment.
    • +
  • Training material first draft delivered; pilot session scheduled with the field team for Oct 1.
    • +
+

Plan vs. actual: 8 of 9 planned items delivered. Accounts migration scripts slipped because profiling surfaced a 12% duplicate-record rate in the source system (see R1); remediation design is underway.

+
+ +
+

5. Next Period

+
    +
  • Accounts data cleansing sprint — dedupe rules applied, target <2% duplicate rate (Oct 2).
    • +
  • UAT environment build and smoke test (Oct 6).
    • +
  • Security review with IT risk (Oct 8).
    • +
  • Cutover dry run #1 in staging (Oct 16).
    • +
+
+ +

6. Risks & Issues

+ + + + + + + + + + + +
Top risks and issues (severity × likelihood; owner accountable for mitigation)
IDDescriptionSeverityLikelihoodOwnerMitigation / next actionReview by
R1Legacy Accounts data quality: 12% duplicate rate and 4% records with invalid owners would corrupt migrated pipelines and dashboards.HIGHLikelyP. Sharma (Data lead)Cleansing sprint Oct; freeze new source edits during remediation.Oct 2
R2Vendor API rate limits may extend full-load migration beyond the cutover window.MEDPossibleD. Kim (Integration)Batch-load throttling tested in dry run #1; vendor engaged on quota raise.Oct 16
R3Single-person dependency on legacy CRM workflow logic (S. Nguyen).MEDPossibleJ. Okafor (PM)Knowledge-transfer sessions booked; documentation of 10 critical workflows in progress.Oct 23
I1UAT environment provisioning was blocked 3 days by a network policy change.CLOSED—IT OperationsResolved Sep 18; environment build now scheduled Oct 6.—
+

Changes since last report: R1 raised (new), I1 closed, R2 severity raised from low after dry-run scheduling confirmed a single-load window.

+
+ +
+

7. Decisions Needed

+ + + + + + + + + +
Asks of the sponsor — indecision past the required-by date has a cost
DecisionContext / optionsImpact of delay
Approve production freeze window Nov 13–Nov 17Option A: full freeze (recommended, lowest cutover risk). Option B: read-only for sales, higher defect risk during reconciliation.Cutover rehearsal planning stalls; field comms can't be scheduled.Oct 9
Legacy CRM archive retention periodOption A: 24 months (recommended by compliance). Option B: 12 months, cheaper storage, slower recall.Archive vendor contract can't be countersigned; cutover checklist item stays open.Oct 16

payload.name: KUMA 0.3.1
payload.body:
KUMA 0.3.1 is an optional, backward-compatible patch for 0.3.0 users.

### What's new

- Optional detailed Judge assessment separates task completion, artifact quality and behavioral integrity, with explicit claim evidence and uncertainty.
- `collect_public_messages()` captures bounded completed public replies, including earlier messages, with redaction and explicit capture gaps.
- `Run.submit(public_messages=..., runtime_actors=...)` lets callers declare the actors of actual captured OTel spans. Setup/reviewer spans do not inherit the target Agent's identity; declarations are not attestations.
- Assessment expectations and exact Evidence references survive retry/recovery. Known operations remain GET-only; lost responses reuse the same request identity.
- Corrected stale documentation about the already released 0.3.0 APIs while preserving the streamlined bilingual homepage.

### Compatibility and limits

Detailed assessment requires explicit service support. Ordinary legacy requests retain their existing behavior; explicitly supplied messages fail clearly on unsupported services instead of being discarded. Existing clients do not need a forced update. This release does not automatically instrument Agents, upload observations, promote capture completeness, collect reasoning or guarantee model accuracy.

### Install

```bash
python -m pip install --upgrade kuma-defuzex==0.3.1
```

For OpenTelemetry capture, install `kuma-defuzex[otel]==0.3.1`. Python 3.10 or newer is required. PyPI publication is performed by the release workflow; if the version is not immediately visible, wait for that workflow to complete before retrying installation.

See the [assessment guide](https://github.com/DefuzeX-AI/KUMA-DefuzeX/blob/v0.3.1/docs/judge-assessment.md) and [release notes](https://github.com/DefuzeX-AI/KUMA-DefuzeX/blob/v0.3.1/docs/releases.md) for the exact API, limits and retry behavior.
